\begin{theorem}[Central limit theorem and closed-form variance for the gauge discrepancy]\label{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-clt}
Under the uniform baseline $\omega\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\Omega_{m+1})$, let $G_m(\omega)$ denote the gauge discrepancy (Definition \ref{def:fold-gauge-anomaly}).
Then there exist constants $g_\ast,\sigma_G^2>0$ such that
\[
\frac{G_m-g_\ast m}{\sqrt m}\Rightarrow \mathcal N(0,\sigma_G^2),
\qquad
\mathrm{Var}(G_m)=\sigma_G^2\,m+o(m).
\]
Moreover, these two constants admit complete closed forms:
\[
\boxed{\ g_\ast=\frac49,\qquad \sigma_G^2=\frac{118}{243}\ }.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch (auditable)]
We use Berstels 4-state unambiguous Zeckendorf normalization transducer (\cite{ITA_2001__35_6_491_0}, Figure~1) to describe bitwise normalization. Under IID Bernoulli$(1/2)$ input, the unique accepting path induces a primitive finite-state Markov chain, and the bitwise gauge-discrepancy indicator $g_t=\mathbf 1\{X_t\neq Y_t\}$ is an additive observable on that chain. Thus the CLT for finite-state Markov chains yields the stated limit theorem.
The constants can be read off from the derivative formulas of the pressure function: assigning edge weights $w_\theta=e^{\theta\,\mathbf 1\{X\neq Y\}}\cdot\mathbb P(X)$ yields the weighted adjacency matrix $A_\theta$; then $P(\theta)=\log\rho(A_\theta)$ satisfies $g_\ast=P'(0)$ and $\sigma_G^2=P''(0)$. The script \texttt{scripts/exp\_fold\_gauge\_anomaly\_clt\_variance.py} implements this computation via exact rational linear algebra and outputs the above closed forms.
\end{proof}
